name_en: Kencho — daikon, tofu, and carrot pan-simmered in a slightly sweet sauce
summary_ja: 豆腐と大根、にんじんをしょうゆと砂糖でやや濃いめに煮る山口の日常菜。大鍋で作って何日も煮返して食べることが多く、由来は鎌倉・建長寺の精進料理にちなむ説が有力とされる。
summary_en: Tofu, daikon, and carrot are pan-simmered in a slightly sweet-savory soy sauce, a daily side dish across Yamaguchi. It is often made in a big pot and reheated over several days, and the name is thought to trace to the vegetarian temple cooking of Kamakura's Kenchoji.
source_title: けんちょう 山口県

name_en: Tsushima — cooked tofu tossed with vegetables in a sweet-vinegar dressing
summary_ja: 炒った豆腐に、だしで煮て下味をつけたにんじんやごぼう、干しえびをあえる周南地域の一皿。生ものを使わず日持ちすることから常備菜として重宝され、来客のもてなしにも用いられてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Pan-cooked tofu is tossed with carrot, burdock, and dried shrimp, each pre-simmered in dashi for flavor—a dish from the Shunan area. Made entirely from cooked ingredients, it keeps well and has long served as both an everyday side and a dish for welcoming guests.

name_en: Ohira — Iwakuni's broth-rich chicken and root vegetable stew
summary_ja: 鶏肉と里芋、れんこんなどを汁多めに煮て、大きな塗り椀「大平」に盛る岩国地域の料理。冠婚葬祭で大人数に振る舞われ、押し寿司の「岩国寿司」と並ぶ祝いの一皿と伝わる。
summary_en: Chicken and root vegetables such as taro and lotus root are simmered in a broth-rich stew and served in a large lacquered bowl called "ohira," the dish's namesake, in the Iwakuni area. Served to crowds at weddings and funerals, it stands alongside the pressed sushi Iwakuni-zushi as an essential celebratory dish.

name_en: Noppei — root vegetables and chicken simmered with a light cornstarch thickening
summary_ja: 里芋やごぼう、れんこんなど冬の根菜を鶏肉とだしで煮て、片栗粉で軽くとろみをつける萩の一皿。仏事に出す際は鶏肉を抜きぎんなんを加えるなど、精進の作法が今も残ると伝わる。
summary_en: Winter root vegetables such as taro, burdock, and lotus root are simmered with chicken in dashi, then lightly thickened with cornstarch—a dish from the castle town of Hagi. For Buddhist memorial meals the chicken is left out and ginkgo nuts added instead, a vegetarian custom still observed.

name_en: Hasu no sanbai — lotus root and carrot dressed in a three-part vinegar sauce
summary_ja: 穴が9つあるのが特徴の岩国れんこんを、にんじんや白身魚とともに三杯酢であえる箸休め。名の由来は調味料の「三杯酢」からとも、田の神「さんばい」からとも言われ、正月や祝いの膳に添えられる。
summary_en: Iwakuni lotus root, notable for having nine holes instead of the usual eight, is dressed with carrot and white fish in a three-part vinegar sauce as a palate cleanser. The name may come from the sanbaizu dressing itself, or from "sanbai," a local word for the rice-field deity, and it appears at New Year and celebratory meals.
source_title: はすのさんばい 山口県

name_en: Nuta — leek and whale tail dressed in sweet white miso vinegar
summary_ja: ねぎとオバイケ（クジラの尾のスライス）を白みそと酢であえる北浦地域の一皿。江戸時代から捕鯨が盛んだったこの地域では鯨肉を余さず使う工夫が根付き、コリコリとした食感が親しまれてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Leek is dressed with obaike—sliced whale tail—in a sweet white-miso vinegar sauce, a dish from the Hokuura coast. Whaling has thrived here since the Edo period, and using every part of the catch became second nature, with the tail's crunchy, gelatinous texture prized in this dish.

name_en: Kujira no nanbanni — whale meat and skin simmered miso-style with chili
summary_ja: クジラの赤身と皮を根菜とともに煮て、赤唐辛子と味噌で仕上げる長門・下関の一皿。長門は江戸時代から続く古い捕鯨の地で、繁栄をもたらしたクジラを弔う法要が今も営まれていると伝わる。
summary_en: Whale meat and skin are simmered with root vegetables, finished with red chili and miso, in this dish from the Nagato and Shimonoseki area. Nagato has whaled since the Edo period, and the memorial rites still held there honor the whales that were said to have brought the town its prosperity.
source_title: くじらの南蛮煮 山口県

name_en: Hasuimo no sunomono — raw lotus-taro stem and grilled horse mackerel in vinegar
summary_ja: れんこんのように小さな穴があく葉柄野菜「はすいも」を生のまま薄切りにし、焼きほぐしたアジと合わせ酢であえる萩の夏の一皿。シャリシャリとした食感が涼を呼ぶと伝わる。
summary_en: Hasuimo, a taro-family stem vegetable riddled with small holes like lotus root, is thinly sliced raw and dressed with vinegar alongside flaked grilled horse mackerel—a summer dish from Hagi. Eaten raw, the stem keeps a crisp, watery crunch said to bring relief from the heat.
source_title: はすいもの酢の物 山口県

name_en: Takenoko no misoni — bamboo shoot pan-simmered in miso until glossy
summary_ja: 乱切りにしたたけのこを油で炒め、味噌と砂糖、しょうゆで汁気がなくなるまで煮詰める山口の春の一皿。岩国の名産として知られるたけのこを使い、家庭料理として親しまれてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Bamboo shoot, cut into large chunks, is pan-fried in oil, then simmered down with miso, sugar, and soy sauce until the liquid is nearly gone—a spring dish in Yamaguchi. It draws on bamboo shoots long known as a specialty of Iwakuni, and has long been a familiar dish on home tables.
source_title: 筍の味噌煮 山口県
